notes.paukwa: The storyteller’s call: shall I tell you?

guidebook.intro: Tell a story the way it’s told around the fire: an opening call, a chain of events and an ending.

tips.title: Opening a story
body: A storyteller may begin with **Mbagambire?** (shall I tell you?) and the listeners answer **Tugambire!** (tell us!). The story starts **Hakaba hariho …** (once there was …).
It ends with **Engano yangye yaahwera aho**, “my story ended there”.

tips.title: And then: mbwenu, ya-
body: Events in a story use the far past **ya-** or **-ka-**: **yaagyenda** (he went), **yaareeba** (he saw), **yaagira** (he said). **Mbwenu** links them: “and so”, “then”. **Aha muheru** means “in the end”.

culture.title: Stories by the fire
body: Grandparents tell **engano**, folk stories, in the evening after the meal. Listeners join in with songs and answers, so a story is a performance, not a reading.
